lifetime_invariants: BUSY reserves exactly one queue insertion; queue insertion accesses only the immortal worker after publication
EXEC/LOOP own the callback; INLINE_QUEUED owns both inline RUN and a separate queued invocation
A queued worker meeting INLINE_QUEUED transfers pending work to inline unlock without executing concurrently
PARKED preserves disabled pending work; shared short state lock serializes parking, enable and running-state observation
No worker dereferences a tasklet after releasing its final running or parked ownership
State spin lock never surrounds callbacks, sleepable queue mutexes or taskqueue_enqueue
Caller must quiesce producers before tasklet_kill/free; disabled pending work must be enabled to drain, as required by Linux tasklet semantics
tasklet.limits: Kernel mutexes, atomics, intrusive queues and worker dispatch are host models; actual NMX taskqueue has its separate fixture. GPU IRQ, real scheduling/preemption and target cleanup remain unverified.

witnesses.route: linux spin_lock -> mtx_lock(MTX_DEF) -> local_bh_disable -> sched_pin -> nmx_critical_enter; nested spin_lock -> native lck_mtx_lock
witnesses.finding: Second acquisition may block with interrupts already masked; real code keeps critical nesting per CPU, invalid if a sleep/migration occurs.

witnesses.route: i915_gem_fence_wait_priority -> local_bh_disable -> engine schedule -> scheduler locks
witnesses.finding: BH masking precedes acquisition even without a preceding spin_lock.

witnesses.route: __intel_engine_flush_submission -> local_bh_disable -> tasklet callback/unlock -> worker queue mutex -> taskqueue_enqueue mutex
witnesses.finding: Tasklet state repair retains real pending work but deliberately does not claim to repair the IRQ-off/sleepable-queue conflict.

witnesses.route: wa_csb_read -> preempt_disable -> intel_uncore_read64 -> fwtable_read64 -> GEN6_READ_HEADER -> spin_lock_irqsave
witnesses.finding: Explicit Linux preemption masking can reach the same native blocking mutex through register reads; changing BH alone is insufficient.
The current adapter can mask interrupts over a hardware polling window up to 50 ms.

witnesses.route: linux_fpu.c fpu_enter -> critical_enter -> per-CPU xsave area -> fpu_leave
witnesses.finding: The native FPU/CPU-local exclusion is real; disabling critical_enter globally would break its ownership contract.
